editorial.headline: Designing Sport and Play, With a Bali PMA Barrier
editorial.standfirst: This code covers industrial design for sports, play and outdoor equipment—nationally open to full foreign ownership, but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Industrial design sits upstream of the finished object: it is the work of creating the product before it reaches a factory, shop floor or playing field. This activity covers industrial design for sports and games equipment, including toys and entertainment products, sports equipment, and tents and outdoor equipment. The design work may also be carried out using specialist software. Its subject is the creation of the product design itself, across play, sport and outdoor use.

The activity is open at every stated business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. Nationally, it is classified as open to PMA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. In practical terms, the national position permits full foreign ownership for this activity; there is no foreign-equity cap below that ceiling in the record. The stated national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali requires a distinctly different reading. A foreign investor is unable to register this activity as PMA in Bali today. At the Besar scale, every scope is assessed in OSS as Low or Medium-Low risk. That places the activity within Bali’s province-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. The restriction is not a partial limitation on ownership: it blocks PMA registration on the island for this activity.

That makes the distinction unusually clear. National openness answers the question of whether foreign ownership is permitted for the activity in Indonesia; for this code, the answer is fully open up to 100%. Bali’s risk-based moratorium answers a separate, local registration question. Because the activity falls within the Low and Medium-Low risk category at the Besar scale across every scope, the Bali route is closed to PMA despite the national foreign-ownership position. Founders considering sports, games or outdoor-equipment design should therefore treat the national permission and the Bali registration outcome as two different facts, both essential and neither interchangeable.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally open to full foreign ownership, this activity is nevertheless blocked from PMA registration in Bali.
